newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar undercut at close by Australian dlr fall.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar undercut at close by Australian dlr fall.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar staged a valiant attempt at a rally back during Tuesday's session, with only a late move down in the Australian dollar taking the gloss off its efforts.
The kiwi was closing at US$0.6745/52 against its 0.6759/66 finish on Monday, after a day of good two-way business in which it traded a 0.6743-57 range.
On its trade-weighted index the kiwi was at 66.30, from 66.08 at the open.
Dealers said volumes had been consistently solid.
The Australian dollar was tripped up late in the piece as the market reacted nervously to comments on interest rates from Prime Minister John Howard.
Howard said one reason why interest rates had come down is that Australia was no longer running such large deficits. He added that he would like to see rates lower yet.
The Australian dollar was closing at US$0.7412/17 against its 0.7443/48 open in New Zealand, and local dealers said Howard's comments had come right when the kiwi was looking particularly strong.
They said the New Zealand dollar was at the mercy of the Australian unit overnight.
